acceptance: Phase 0 stopgap: read() sweeps old revs best-effort under a non-blocking flock, keeping the tip, the rev `last` names and revs modified in the last 10 minutes, capped per call, renaming victims to trash before removal.
The snapshot cache is a bare git object store per namespace (<cache>/<ns>/store.git) fetched incrementally by URL with no configured remote; reads build snapshots from objects and never write revs/.
refs/todo-db/tip replaces the `last` pointer and is updated by compare-and-swap; it never moves backwards except to follow a rewritten remote branch.
Store growth after maintenance is at most 2x the raw bytes of the items touched, and unpacked slack between maintenance runs is capped (8 MiB), enforced by a detached, locked repack + prune.
mutate, restore_rev, read_rev, history and reconcile run against the store; plumbing-built commits match the worktree path in tree OID and commit body.
Offline reads serve the store tip, falling back to legacy revs/<last> until the store has a tip.
`todo-db cache prune` removes legacy revs/, last files, stale tmp files, 40-hex dirs and unused namespaces, and runs maintenance; never part of read().
Multi-process tests cover concurrent reads and mutations during maintenance, offline reads after maintenance, and the size bound.
Git >= 2.29 is required for the store; older git falls back to the temp-repo path.
context: Plan approved 2026-10-17: replace the per-rev snapshot cache with a git object store (phases 0-4). Measured on BenchBox todo-state: full history packs to 14 MiB, ~1.8 KB per commit vs ~5 KB of items touched. Branch feat/git-object-store-cache.
description:
read() caches every new state-branch tip as a full snapshot under <cache>/<ns>/revs/<sha>/ and never deletes old ones. Only the resolved tip and the rev named by `last` are ever read back, so the rest is dead weight. The BenchBox namespace (e688dcd1868ed3f8) held 1,508 revs, about 40 GiB, on 2026-10-16 and grows by up to about 3 GiB a day.

An adversarial review rejected the first proposal (keep only the new tip and the previous `last`): the first sweep would delete ~40 GiB inside read() and exceed the git and MCP timeouts; `last` is written by every process and is not monotonic, so the rule can delete the true newest tip; deleting a rev while another process is in save_snapshot raises a raw FileNotFoundError out of read(); _offline_cached has no fallback for a missing or partial rev.
